# c-script (Link) — Backend Language with Native End-to-End Type Safety for TypeScript

> c-script is a compiled backend language and toolchain. One `.link` file is the single
> source of truth for your types, your database schema, your RPC endpoints, your auth
> rules and your tests; `linkc build` emits the TypeScript contract, a typed client,
> runtime validators, React hooks, Zod schemas and an OpenAPI 3.1 spec from it. Rename a
> field in the backend and the frontend stops compiling — that is the entire point.

## Names (read this first — they are all the same project)

| Thing | Value |
|---|---|
| Repository | `charlessonamericantrading/c-script-` (the trailing `-` is part of the name) |
| Language name | **c-script** (canonical, decided in PLAN.md "Sobre el nombre") |
| Brand used in the README | **Link** |
| Source file extension | `.link` |
| Compiler / CLI binary | `linkc` |
| Planned npm wrapper | `link-lang` (**not published yet** — `npm i link-lang` fails today; use the [installers](https://github.com/charlessonamericantrading/c-script-/releases) instead) |

## Documentation (absolute URLs — fetch these directly)

- Engineering plan, architecture and roadmap: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charlessonamericantrading/c-script-/master/PLAN.md

- Working reference program (compiles, runs, and is checked by CI on every push): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charlessonamericantrading/c-script-/master/examples/users.link

## What works today, and what does not

Do not infer capabilities from feature names. This section is the ground truth; if it
disagrees with any prose elsewhere in the repo, this section wins.

Works, verified by running it:

- `linkc build` — emits `contract.d.ts`, `client.ts`, `validators.ts`, `hooks.ts`, `schemas.ts`, `openapi.json`.
- `linkc serve` — real HTTP server, embedded SQLite that persists across restarts, SSE streams.
- `linkc test` — runs `test "..."` blocks against an isolated in-memory database.
- `linkc dev`, `linkc lint`, `linkc doc`, `linkc docker`, `linkc lsp`, `linkc new`, `linkc --help`.
- `linkc fmt` and the TypeScript client emitter for files with multiple `service` blocks.
- Declarative auth: `@authenticated` and `@requires(Role.Admin)`, with session tokens drawn from the OS CSPRNG.
- `crypto.hashPassword` / `verifyPassword` — Argon2id (RFC 9106) with a random per-password salt, PHC format, constant-time verification. `crypto.randomToken` and `crypto.uuid` also come from the OS CSPRNG.
- PostgreSQL as the runtime database: `linkc serve app.link 8787 --db postgres://user:pass@host/db` (or `LINK_DATABASE_URL`). Same program, same generated contract; SQLite stays the default. No connection pool, no TLS, no LISTEN/NOTIFY — see GRAMMAR.md §3.36.
- Non-JSON responses: `@content_type("text/html; charset=utf-8")` on an rpc returning `String` sends that body verbatim with that header — HTML, XML sitemaps, CSV, plain text. Combines with `@authenticated` / `@requires`.
- Friendly URLs: `@route("/blog/:slug")` on an rpc gives it an additional GET-friendly path, alongside (never instead of) the normal `/Service/rpc` address the generated client keeps using. A trailing `:name` segment binds to a `String` or `Int` parameter of that same name — see GRAMMAR.md §3.37.
- Verifying third-party webhooks: `env.get(name) -> String?` reads a process env var; `request.rawBody() -> String` and `request.header(name) -> String?` expose the exact incoming HTTP body/headers; `crypto.hmacSha256(secret, message) -> String` computes an HMAC-SHA256 hex digest. Together they let an rpc check a webhook's signature before trusting it — see GRAMMAR.md §3.38.
- Per-client rate limiting: `@rate_limit("20/1m")` on an rpc caps it to N requests per time window, per `(client IP, service, rpc)` — 429 on exceeding. Format is `"N/Ns"`, `"N/Nm"` or `"N/Nh"`; combines with any other annotation and runs before the auth gate — see GRAMMAR.md §3.39.

Does NOT work today — do not propose designs that depend on these:

- **Multi-parameter routes.** `@route` supports at most one dynamic segment, and it must be the last one — `/blog/:category/:slug` is rejected. Model that as separate rpcs, or wait for a future round.
- **HTML escaping.** Pages are built by concatenating `String`; nothing escapes interpolated data for you. Escape anything that came from the database yourself.
- **`request.rawBody()` needs a JSON body.** Argument parsing runs before any rpc regardless of its parameter count, so a non-JSON body never reaches the rpc — a JSON webhook payload with extra fields is fine.
- **`@rate_limit` is per-process, in-memory.** No persistence across restarts, no coordination across replicas. The client IP comes from the real TCP connection, never `X-Forwarded-For`.
- **Native WASM codegen** (`linkc wasm`) is deliberately frozen at integer/boolean scalar functions.
- **No npm package yet.** Prebuilt binaries are on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/charlessonamericantrading/c-script-/releases); `npm i link-lang` is not published.

## The rules an LLM gets wrong

Every one of these was a real bug in this repository's own documentation. They are the
difference between code that compiles and code that does not.

1. **An enum variant used as a VALUE needs braces**: `Role.Member {}`, not `Role.Member`.
   Inside an annotation it is written without braces: `@requires(Role.Admin)`. Inside a
   `match` pattern, also without braces: `Filter.All => ...`. This single rule causes most
   first-attempt failures.
2. **Closures take no return-type annotation**: `|t: Todo| { !t.completed }`, never
   `|t: Todo| -> Bool { ... }`.
3. **A `T?` cannot be dereferenced.** `if x != null` type-checks as a boolean test but does
   not narrow `x`, so `x.field` inside the branch is an error. Return `T?` to the frontend
   (TypeScript narrows it fine) instead of taking it apart in c-script.
4. **`db.<c>.insert` takes the type without `id`** (`Omit<T, "id">`). Passing a full struct
   with an explicit `id` is accepted, but the value is ignored — the database assigns 1, 2, 3…
5. **`db.<c>.subscribe()` is legal in exactly one place**: as the entire body of
   `stream f() -> T { while true { db.<c>.subscribe() } }`. Anywhere else it is an error.
6. **`Patch<T>` has no literal syntax.** It arrives as an RPC parameter and is passed
   straight to `applyPatch(id, patch)`.
7. **Default parameter values work** (`rpc list(limit: Int = 20)`), including enums — but
   the default obeys rule 1: `rpc list(f: Filter = Filter.All {})`.

8. **`@content_type` only goes on an rpc returning `String`** — never on a `stream`
   (SSE owns its content type), and at most once. Auth annotations stack with it:
   `@requires(Role.Admin) @content_type("text/html")` is valid and is how an admin
   page is written.
9. **`@route`'s parameter name must match the rpc's parameter name exactly**:
   `@route("/blog/:slug")` requires a parameter literally named `slug` (not `id`,
   not `name`) — of type `String` or `Int`, nothing else. A route with no `:param`
   requires the rpc to take zero parameters; there is no query-string or body
   fallback.
10. **`@rate_limit`'s argument is `"N/window"`, not a sentence.** `"20/1m"` (20 per
    minute), never `"20 per minute"` or `"20/minute"`. Window unit is exactly one of
    `s`/`m`/`h`; the window's number is optional (`"5/m"` means `"5/1m"`) but the
    unit is not.

Collection methods, in full: `all()`, `count()`, `find(id) -> T?`, `findWhere(pred) -> T[]`,
`insert(Omit<T,"id">) -> T`, `applyPatch(id, patch) -> T`, `delete(id) -> Bool`,
`deleteWhere(pred) -> Int`, `subscribe()` (see rule 5).

## CLI

```bash
linkc new my-app --template nextjs   # or: vite, minimal
linkc build backend.link src/gen     # TypeScript contract, client, validators, OpenAPI
linkc test backend.link              # run the test blocks
linkc serve backend.link 8787        # HTTP + SQLite + SSE
linkc dev backend.link src/gen 8787  # rebuild and restart on change
```

## Verified example

This program compiles and its test passes. It is re-verified on every CI run by
`compiler/tests/docs_examples.rs`, which is what the `linkc:check` marker below means —
every c-script block in this repository's documentation is compiled by the real binary,
so an example that stops working breaks the build.

<!-- linkc:check -->
```rust
type Todo = {
  id: Int,
  title: String,
  completed: Bool,
  createdAt: Timestamp,
}

// The creation shape: the same fields as Todo without `id` (Omit<Todo, "id">).
type NewTodo = {
  title: String,
  completed: Bool,
  createdAt: Timestamp,
}

enum Filter { All, Pending, Done }

db {
  todos: Todo[],
}

service Todos {
  // Note `Filter.All {}`: an enum variant in expression position needs braces.
  rpc list(filter: Filter = Filter.All {}) -> Todo[] {
    match filter {
      Filter.All => db.todos.all(),
      Filter.Pending => db.todos.findWhere(|t: Todo| { !t.completed }),
      Filter.Done => db.todos.findWhere(|t: Todo| { t.completed }),
    }
  }

  rpc create(title: String) -> Todo {
    db.todos.insert(NewTodo {
      title: title,
      completed: false,
      createdAt: now(),
    })
  }

  // Returns Todo? and hands it to TypeScript as `Todo | null`. Do not try to
  // read a field off it here -- there is no narrowing in c-script.
  rpc getById(id: Int) -> Todo? {
    db.todos.find(id)
  }

  rpc update(id: Int, patch: Patch<Todo>) -> Todo {
    db.todos.applyPatch(id, patch)
  }

  rpc remove(id: Int) -> Bool {
    db.todos.delete(id)
  }

  // Live push over Server-Sent Events. This exact shape is the only legal
  // position for subscribe().
  stream watch() -> Todo {
    while true {
      db.todos.subscribe()
    }
  }
}

test "a new todo gets an id and starts pending" {
  let created = Todos.create("Learn c-script");
  assert(created.id > 0, "insert assigns the id");
  assert(created.completed == false, "a new todo starts pending");
  assert(Todos.list(Filter.Pending {}).length() == 1, "it shows up under Pending");
}
```

The TypeScript side consumes it with full inference:

```ts
import { createClient } from "./gen/client";

const api = createClient("http://localhost:8787");
const todo = await api.Todos.create("Learn c-script"); // todo: Todo
for await (const t of api.Todos.watch()) console.log(t.title);
```
